title: Week 12 · Overview — The sample arm · Hydraulic claws
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, March 1, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 3: Sense it — Fluids, Waves & Electromagnetism · fluids-pressure · Core week

El brazo de muestras · Garras hidráulicas

The week in one paragraph

A spacecraft that visits 2026-XJ needs an arm — and an arm needs force multiplication. The shop's version is syringes and tubing. Push the small one; the big one moves with more force and less distance. Predict the ratio from the diameters before you measure it.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can define pressure as force over area and use it with real syringe sizes.Puedo definir la presión como fuerza sobre área y usarla con tamaños reales de jeringa.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can explain that pressure is the same everywhere in the tube, so a small syringe can push a big one.Puedo explicar que la presión es la misma en todo el tubo, así que una jeringa pequeña puede empujar una grande.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can predict the force multiplication from the two syringe diameters and measure it.Puedo predecir la multiplicación de fuerza a partir de los dos diámetros de jeringa y medirla.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can show that what you gain in force you pay in distance — work in equals work out.Puedo mostrar que lo que ganas en fuerza lo pagas en distancia — el trabajo de entrada es igual al de salida.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
SpeakingSay "small pushes big" with the syringes in hand.Explain force multiplication and the distance cost.Digo "pequeño empuja grande" con las jeringas.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
Phase 3 opens: the mission needs an arm, an ear and an actuator. First the arm.Pascal's principle is force multiplication that costs distance — work in equals work out. The claw that lifts a known mass is the sample arm at desk scale.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 1 Mar		Measure syringe diameters; predict force ratio; lock itLocked prediction
2
Tue 2 Mar		Measure force in vs. out with two force sensors; distances tooForce and distance table
3
Wed 3 Mar		Build the claw (3–4 syringes)Timeline entry
4
Thu 4 Mar		Claw challenge: lift a known mass; work in vs. work outWork in / work out
5
Fri 5 Mar		Reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Your predicted force multiplication from the diameters, the measured one, and the reconciliation with distance — work in vs. work out.

Tu multiplicación de fuerza predicha a partir de los diámetros, la medida, y la reconciliación con la distancia — trabajo de entrada vs. trabajo de salida.

Off-week question

Find a hydraulic system at work (a jack, a lift, a brake). Which cylinder is small and which is big, and why that way round?

Encuentra un sistema hidráulico en el trabajo (un gato, un elevador, un freno). ¿Qué cilindro es pequeño y cuál es grande, y por qué en ese orden?

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Syringes (two sizes), tubing, craft sticks, two Vernier force sensors

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1syringe (noun)jeringaA tube with a plunger.Push the small syringe.
1lift (verb)levantarRaise something up.The claw lifts the mass.
2multiply (verb)multiplicar ≈Make bigger by a factor.The big syringe multiplies the force.
2ratio (noun)razón / proporción (≠ ratio)One number compared to another, like 4 to 1.Predict the force ratio from the diameters.
3pressure (noun)presión ≈Force spread over an area.Pressure is the same everywhere in the tube.
3area (noun)área ≈How much surface, in cm².A bigger area means more force at the same pressure.
3hydraulic (adjective)hidráulico ≈Working by pushing a liquid.A hydraulic claw uses water in tubes.
3Pascal's principle (noun)principio de Pascal ≈Pressure in a trapped liquid is the same everywhere.Pascal's principle is why small pushes big.

Beck tiers: 3 is the physics word, 2 is the academic verb the frames are built from, 1 is the everyday word the demonstration needs. ≈ marks a cognate — say it as one out loud. ≠ marks a false friend — name the trap before it bites. Never introduce a word without the object in hand.

Standards

HS-PS2-1, HS-ETS1-3

Where this week lands — Phase 3 mastery task

This week's artifact is evidence toward pp.t3.mastery-chain-of-cause, the Phase 3 mastery task. The full task is on the overview for the last week of this phase.

The rules that do not change

  1. Hands first, always. The block opens with the object doing the thing. The explanation arrives after there is a result to explain — never a mini-lecture the build is waiting behind.
  2. The prediction is locked before the test, and it is scored on the reasoning, never on being right.
  3. The reasoning artifact is the grade. Whether the bridge held is recorded on its own product target and is never folded into the reasoning score.
  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.
  5. Nothing is graded that a WIDA Level 1 student could not have reached. Walk the artifact as that student before you rate anyone.

Full spec: the SEI access layer and the year map in the Claude project. The four-segment block — hands · record · talk · write, about 25 minutes each — is the shape of every meeting.

No day-by-day plans written for this week yet. Say the word and they get the same treatment as Weeks 1 and 2: segment timings and materials, the Spanish for the day, the formative checks and the misconception to press.

title: Week 13 · Overview — The ear · Record player and megaphone
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, March 15, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 3: Sense it — Fluids, Waves & Electromagnetism · waves-sound · Core week

El oído · Tocadiscos y megáfono

The week in one paragraph

An impact anywhere on Earth is a pressure wave first — and every instrument that senses one is reading a wave. A paper cone, a pin, a record spun by hand: music comes out. Then a megaphone. What is the cone doing to the groove's motion, and to the air?

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can name amplitude, frequency and wavelength on a sound trace and say what each sounds like.Puedo nombrar amplitud, frecuencia y longitud de onda en un registro de sonido y decir cómo suena cada una.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can explain the chain from a groove wiggling a needle to air pressure at my ear.Puedo explicar la cadena desde el surco que mueve la aguja hasta la presión del aire en mi oído.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can predict how cone size changes loudness or pitch, then test it.Puedo predecir cómo el tamaño del cono cambia el volumen o el tono, y luego probarlo.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can explain why a cone or tube makes some frequencies louder than others.Puedo explicar por qué un cono o tubo hace algunas frecuencias más fuertes que otras.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
Sensing means reading waves. The analysts read 2026-XJ by radar; the shop starts with sound because you can hold it.Groove → needle → cone → air → ear is a chain of cause, one link per sentence. Amplitude, frequency and resonance are the words every sensor engineer uses.

DayHands (first)Into the app

¿Dónde en tu taller hay mucho ruido, y qué forma tiene el espacio? ¿Cambiaría con otra forma?

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1loud (adjective)fuerteA big sound.A bigger cone is louder.

title: Week 14 · Overview — The actuator · World's simplest motor
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, March 29, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 3: Sense it — Fluids, Waves & Electromagnetism · electromagnetism · Core week

El actuador · El motor más simple del mundo

The week in one paragraph

Spacecraft point themselves with motors — reaction wheels, gimbals. The shop's motor is a battery, a magnet and a bent wire. It spins. Before the first spin: which way? Then flip the magnet — which way now?

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can show that a current makes a magnetic field, with a compass.Puedo mostrar que una corriente crea un campo magnético, con una brújula.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can explain that a current in a magnetic field feels a force, and which way.Puedo explicar que una corriente en un campo magnético siente una fuerza, y en qué dirección.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can predict the direction of rotation from the field and current, then reverse one and predict again.Puedo predecir la dirección de giro a partir del campo y la corriente, luego invertir uno y predecir de nuevo.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can explain why the motor keeps turning instead of stopping at one position.Puedo explicar por qué el motor sigue girando en lugar de detenerse en una posición.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
SpeakingSay "left" or "right" as a prediction, then "yes" or "no."Explain the direction rule.Digo "izquierda" o "derecha" antes de girar.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
An arm and an ear so far. Now the thing that moves the spacecraft's parts: current in a magnetic field feels a force.Predicting the direction of rotation from field and current — then reversing one — is the reasoning behind every actuator on the mission.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app

Mon 29 Mar		Compass next to a current-carrying wire; field directionCompass sketches
2

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Three predictions of rotation direction (original, magnet flipped, battery flipped), each made before the spin, and an explanation of why it keeps turning.

Tres predicciones de la dirección de giro (original, imán invertido, batería invertida), cada una hecha antes de girar, y una explicación de por qué sigue girando.

Off-week question

Find a motor at work. Where is the magnet, and where does the current go in?

Encuentra un motor en el trabajo. ¿Dónde está el imán y por dónde entra la corriente?

AA batteries, neodymium magnets, copper wire, compasses

title: Week 15 · Overview — Communications · Build a speaker
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, April 12, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 3: Sense it — Fluids, Waves & Electromagnetism · electromagnetism · Core week

Comunicaciones · Construye un altavoz

The week in one paragraph

A signal from the spacecraft becomes motion becomes a wave: that is a speaker, and it is the motor and the record player in one object. Coil, magnet, cup, a phone. Sound. Say how — one link per sentence — then change one thing and predict what it does.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can explain how a changing current in the coil makes a changing force on the magnet.Puedo explicar cómo una corriente cambiante en la bobina produce una fuerza cambiante sobre el imán.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can explain how the cone's motion becomes a pressure wave in the air.Puedo explicar cómo el movimiento del cono se convierte en una onda de presión en el aire.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can write the causal chain from signal to sound, one link per sentence, with no link missing.Puedo escribir la cadena causal desde la señal hasta el sonido, un eslabón por oración, sin que falte ninguno.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can predict which change (more turns, stronger magnet, lighter cone) helps, then test it.Puedo predecir qué cambio (más vueltas, imán más fuerte, cono más ligero) ayuda, y luego probarlo.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
WritingDraw the chain with arrows and label it from the word bank.Write the chain, one link per sentence.Dibujo la cadena con flechas y etiquetas.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
The motor (force from a current) and the ear (a pressure wave) meet in a speaker.The causal chain from signal to sound is the same chain as a radio receiver's — the mission's comms in a paper cup.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 12 Apr		Wind the coil, mount on the cup, magnet behind; first soundSketch with parts labeled
2
Tue 13 Apr		Chain of cause from signal to soundChain page
3
Wed 14 Apr		Predict which ONE change helps loudness; lock; measure with the microphonePredicted / actual
4
Thu 15 Apr		Second variable if time; compare to the motor and the record playerComparison table
5
Fri 16 Apr		Reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

The causal chain from signal to sound with no link missing, and your tested prediction about the one design change you made.

La cadena causal desde la señal hasta el sonido sin que falte ningún eslabón, y tu predicción probada sobre el único cambio de diseño que hiciste.

Off-week question

Look at a speaker grille at work or in a car. Estimate the cone size. What would a bigger one do better and worse?

Mira la rejilla de un altavoz en el trabajo o en un carro. Estima el tamaño del cono. ¿Qué haría mejor y peor uno más grande?

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Magnet wire, neodymium magnets, paper cups, 3.5 mm cable, Vernier microphone

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1coil (noun)bobinaWire wound in loops.Wind the coil on the cup.
1cup (noun)vasoThe paper cone that moves the air.The cup is the speaker's cone.
2signal (noun)señalA changing current that carries sound.The phone sends a signal to the coil.
2cause (noun)causa ≈What makes something happen.Write the cause of each link.
3electromagnet (noun)electroimánA coil that becomes a magnet when current flows.The coil is an electromagnet.
3pressure wave (noun)onda de presión ≈Sound: a wave of pushed air.The cone makes a pressure wave.
3speaker (noun)altavoz / bocinaA device that turns a signal into sound.Our speaker is a coil, a magnet and a cup.
3variable (noun)variable ≈The one thing you change.Change one variable: turns, magnet or cone.

Beck tiers: 3 is the physics word, 2 is the academic verb the frames are built from, 1 is the everyday word the demonstration needs. ≈ marks a cognate — say it as one out loud. ≠ marks a false friend — name the trap before it bites. Never introduce a word without the object in hand.

Standards

HS-PS2-5, HS-PS3-3

Where this week lands — Phase 3 mastery task

You are given a device that uses pressure, sound or electromagnetism — one you have not seen opened — and asked to open it, draw it, and write the chain of cause from input to output with no link missing. Then predict what one change would do and, if the device allows, test it.

Te dan un dispositivo que usa presión, sonido o electromagnetismo — uno que no has visto abierto — y te piden abrirlo, dibujarlo y escribir la cadena causal desde la entrada hasta la salida sin que falte ningún eslabón. Luego predice qué haría un cambio y, si el dispositivo lo permite, pruébalo.

DimensionWhat a 3 looks like
ScienceEvery link in the chain is physically correct — pressure, wave or field — and named with the right word.
ReasoningNo link is missing or magic; the predicted effect of the change follows from the chain.
CommunicationThe drawing carries the chain; the sentences carry the causes. Either language.
TransferA device not built in class, explained with the physics of the claw, the cone and the motor.

Walk this task as a Level 1 student before it ships: can the prompt be understood from the diagram and the Spanish alone, and can every dimension be met with labels, a frame, numbers and a spoken defence in Spanish? If any answer is no, it is not ready.

  2. The prediction is locked before the test, and it is scored on the reasoning, never on being right.
  3. The reasoning artifact is the grade. Whether the bridge held is recorded on its own product target and is never folded into the reasoning score.
  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.
  5. Nothing is graded that a WIDA Level 1 student could not have reached. Walk the artifact as that student before you rate anyone.
